items.headline: Claude reaches general availability in Microsoft Foundry on Azure-hosted NVIDIA GB300
items.diff_narrative: This story did not appear in yesterday's slate, which led on Micron's HBM sold-out quarter. Today's lead reports that Anthropic and Microsoft moved Claude from preview to general availability inside Microsoft Foundry on June 29, shipping Claude Opus 4.8 and Haiku 4.5 through the Messages API with prompt caching and extended thinking, an Azure-hosted GA tier and an Anthropic-hosted preview tier, consolidated billing, and an Azure-hosted path running on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems with Quantum-X800 InfiniBand. Where yesterday's hardware angle was memory supply gating GPU buildout, today's frame is the consolidation of the PaaS-LLM layer, with a frontier lab's flagship models now running on the hyperscaler's own silicon inside the customer's tenant.

items.headline: vLLM ships v0.24.0 with quantized-by-default Model Runner V2 and multi-tier KV-cache offloading
items.diff_narrative: No counterpart existed in yesterday's slate, which covered Qualcomm's Dragonfly roadmap on the hardware side rather than the serving stack. Today introduces vLLM v0.24.0 (571 commits, 256 contributors): Model Runner V2 now defaults to quantized models, a multi-tier KV-cache offloading path adds an object-store tier for spilling beyond GPU memory, DeepSeek-V4 gets a sparse index cache and prefill chunk-planning, DeepEP v2 lands for MoE expert parallelism, and the Rust frontend matures with auth, CORS and a unified tool-call/reasoning streaming parser, alongside SM90 CUTLASS FP8 speedups and launch-day coverage for MiniMax-M3, DiffusionGemma and Gemma 4. This shifts the throughput-per-dollar conversation from yesterday's silicon-roadmap framing toward the open-source inference layer itself.

items.headline: WorldEvolver arxiv paper on self-evolving world models for LLM-agent planning
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday carried no research item; its third slot was Gartner's agent-spend forecast paired with the Sarvam unicorn. Today adds a June 29 arXiv submission, "Self-Evolving World Models for LLM Agent Planning," proposing WorldEvolver, which sharpens agents' action-outcome prediction through episodic memory, semantic memory that distills rules from prediction errors, and a selective-foresight filter. The distinguishing design is that the world model keeps updating at inference time while the agent backbone stays frozen; the authors report top prediction accuracy across three backbones and higher task-success rates than competing baselines, positioning runtime memory updates as a cheaper reliability lever than fine-tuning for the agent harnesses today's other items also touch.

items.headline: AI events tracker across mainstream, security and chip sub-tracks
items.diff_narrative: The events tracker carries over from yesterday but advances the AI Engineer World's Fair from its opening day to mid-run: where yesterday described the main program opening with the Coding Agents keynote, today places it mid-event at Moscone West with the Autoresearch keynote and ~12 parallel tracks on July 1 and the Harness Engineering keynote on July 2, and adds an expo-partner count (~100). The standing summer and fall dates are unchanged and carried forward — GitHub Universe (Oct 28-29), AWS re:Invent (Nov 30-Dec 4), the AI Risk Summit (Aug 11-12), Black Hat and DEF CON 34, OWASP Global AppSec (Nov 5-6), the Zenity series watch, AMD Advancing AI (July 22-23), Hot Chips (Aug 23-25) and the AI Infra Summit (Sep 15-17) — with the framing still an attendance planner tying the security and chip tracks to the secure-accelerator and agent-hijack threads.
